costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 1KD-FTV typically takes 10-14 hours at £65/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.

A unit with documented injector seal replacements and EGR cleaning will command a slight premium but offers significantly lower long-term risk for high-mileage commercial or off-road use. failures.title: Toyota 1KD-FTV Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Injector Seal Failure ("Black Death") - 2004-2015
items.whatHappens: The copper washer seals at the base of the injectors degrade over time, allowing combustion gases to escape. This creates a thick, black, tar-like carbon buildup around the injector head, which can eventually corrode the cylinder head or cause persistent misfires.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the injector seals is a routine and relatively inexpensive maintenance task (£500-£1,500). Full 1KD-FTV engine replacement is only required if prolonged neglect has caused severe head corrosion or cracked injectors.

items.title: EGR and DPF Clogging - 2004-2015
items.whatHappens: Frequent short trips or urban driving prevent the DPF from regenerating, while the EGR valve accumulates soot. This leads to restricted airflow, reduced power, and illuminated warning lights on the dashboard.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR cleaning or replacement and DPF regeneration are standard repairs. A full 1KD-FTV engine replacement is rarely needed unless severe overheating or runaway conditions have occurred due to blocked systems.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 1KD-FTV is widely regarded as one of Toyota’s most robust modern diesel engines. While early pre-2007 units had slightly more EGR sensitivity, the core architecture remains highly durable, with many examples exceeding 200,000 miles with proper maintenance .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 1KD-FTV
variants.intro: The 1KD-FTV engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically near the oil filter housing or on the front timing cover, and is also listed in section V.5 of your V5C logbook. It is sometimes confused with the older 1KZ-TE (which is indirect injection and lacks a high-pressure common rail system) or the newer 1GD-FTV (the 2.8L D-4D successor). Fitting the wrong engine or ECU will result in severe performance issues, as the 1KD-FTV relies on specific common-rail calibration and turbocharger mapping that are not interchangeable with other Toyota diesel families.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 1KD-FTV - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 1KD-FTV engine is a viable option for older Hilux or Land Cruiser models, provided it comes with a verifiable service history confirming the injector seals and EGR have been maintained. Given its commercial legend status, low-mileage used units are highly sought after, so ensure the seller can prove the mileage and absence of "Black Death" carbon buildup.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned 1KD-FTV replaces all wear-prone components, including the injector seals, EGR valve, and turbocharger seals, while retaining the original robust block. This is the recommended route for most owners, balancing cost with long-term reliability for demanding off-road or commercial use.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if the original 1KD-FTV suffered catastrophic failure, such as a snapped timing chain or severe overheating. A specialist rebuild can also include upgraded head gaskets and pistons to safely handle future heavy towing or extreme off-road conditions.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota 1KD-FTV engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned Toyota 1KD-FTV engine costs between £1,800 and £3,500 for supply only. Fitted prices typically range from £2,450 to £4,410 at an independent specialist, while used 1KD-FTV units are available from £600 but require careful injector seal inspection.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common problem with the 1KD-FTV engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most documented failure pattern for the 1KD-FTV is injector seal degradation, commonly known as Black Death. Copper washer seals at the injector base fail between 80,000 and 150,000 miles, creating thick carbon buildup around the injector head which can corrode the cylinder head if left untreated.

mainEntity.name: Which Toyota models use the 1KD-FTV engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1KD-FTV 3.0 D-4D is fitted to two primary Toyota model lines in the UK. The Toyota Hilux Mk7 and Mk8 (2004-2015) is the highest-volume application, and the Toyota Land Cruiser J120 and J150 Prado (2004-2015) also uses this engine.

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 1KD-FTV engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned 1KD-FTV is the recommended choice for most Hilux and Land Cruiser owners. Proper reconditioning addresses the known injector seal and EGR weaknesses specific to this engine, whereas used units are viable only with verifiable service history confirming the Black Death carbon buildup has been addressed.

mainEntity.name: How do I confirm my vehicle has the 1KD-FTV engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can confirm your vehicle has the 1KD-FTV by checking section V.5 of your V5C registration document. The code is also physically stamped on the engine block near the oil filter housing or front timing cover, and is commonly confused with the older 1KZ-TE or the newer 1GD-FTV, which are not interchangeable.
